prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1228; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured. Insured states vehicles made contact at low speed in a traffic lane. Both drivers reported as ambulatory at scene. Photos requested from insured and the other driver's carrier. Liability appears disputed pending police report.

Entry 2: Police report received. Investigating officer notes minimal visible damage to both vehicles and a single contact point at the front bumpers. Other driver cites sudden stop by the insured as the cause. Recorded statement scheduled with the insured. Liability still under review.

Entry 3: Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness following the collision and has sought treatment at an urgent care facility. Diagnosis on file is whiplash-type soft tissue injury. Claimant has retained counsel, who has requested that all further contact be directed to the firm. Future communications will be routed accordingly.

Entry 4: Received letter of representation from claimant's attorney. Requested medical records and billing from treating providers through counsel. Reviewed vehicle photos; repair estimates indicate low-severity damage consistent with reported impact speed. Bodily injury evaluation on hold until records are complete.

Entry 5: Medical records received through counsel and reviewed. Treatment consists of conservative care including physical therapy, with no imaging findings of fracture. Treating physician notes expected recovery timeline of several weeks. Demand package not yet received. Reserves reviewed and file referred to supervisor for evaluation of settlement authority once demand is submitted.
